title: Visual Hallucination Under Over‐Conducted Survival Efforts
content: Visual hallucination is a debilitating symptom of many mental illnesses. This paper dives into the mechanisms behind visual perception. We suggest that vision perception can be understood as sequential biomolecular activations, and the activations of these pre-existing molecular machineries in fact are independent from light sensing, suggesting vision perception does not necessarily rely on light signals. We further highlight that the observed aberrant neuronal activities - ‘misfiring’ in visual hallucinations, represent ‘self-enforced’ cellular activities in response to endangered survival, reflecting an intrinsic recovery strategy typically adopted during human dreaming but exaggeratedly executed in response to severely compromised cellular machinery that exceeds normal endurance. The idea nuancedly shifts the current focus on abnormal neuronal activities in visual hallucination, to the cause of such abnormal activities. Our paper adds further insights into current treatment options for patients experiencing ‘visual hallucination’ by reframing the current focus to the essential molecular machinery rooted for normal vision and underlying these aberrant activities.
